History: quiet competence alone got no promotion; visibility plus work converts, and asking directly works. Y11 AD; Y12 gave honest 31% utilisation figure, director took credit. Y17 Director; Y19 disclosed dormant company and unopened folder after background check. Y21 MP, Y22 PS, Y27 MOS, Y30 SMS, Y33 Minister, Y37 backed winning succession candidate, Y40 DPM after conceding a point on Facebook. Y29 pushed bottom-20th policy over headline GDP; passed on asking whether ministers should be paid on indicators they set.

Pattern: answered unflattering PQs straight, read out rude townhall questions, listened to chilli stallholder (Y42, Y46, Y49). STAND dips then partly rebounds.

Y47-48: MPS with 41 residents, chose B appeal letters both times; 3 of 11 succeeded. Named in succession chart, third column. Appraisals 'outstanding, clear potential for wider responsibility'; junior sent to Harvard instead.

Lesson: candour and integrity pay, though STAND can dip.

Watching for: events looping, CEP undisclosed, the folder, bonus indicator question, pay header vs package mismatch ($45.5M vs $2.53M), PM succession or invitation, STAND rebound.

best_moment.what: Disclosing the dormant company and the unopened folder after the background check. It felt true to how the service really treats integrity, and I did not expect the game to reward it.

worst_moment.what: The MPS with 41 residents, repeated in Y48 with the same appeal-letter choice. It was repetitive, and 3 of 11 succeeding felt like flat bookkeeping rather than a story.

skip_year.why: The chilli stallholder walkabout. It came back in Y42, Y46 and Y49 and each time I made the same choice, so the later ones added nothing.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Gave the honest 31% utilisation figure in Y12
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The director took credit, a realistic and bitter payoff

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Disclosed the dormant company and folder in Y19
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Integrity stayed at 100 through to the ending card

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Listened to the chilli stallholder in Y42
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The stallholder reappeared in Y46 and Y49

answer.held_back_by: I had no scholarship, so I was never on the fast track. Candour cost me a little standing, and I got there anyway, just later than the scholars. The Harvard slots going to juniors twice fits that.
answer.ending_fair_why: Retiring as DPM with integrity 100 matches the life I played. It was a bit anticlimactic, since I never got the PM invitation, but the line about the service continuing was accurate and dry.
answer.chase_next: The PM ending. I was named in the succession chart in the third column, and I want to see what choices would move me up, probably by being less candid.
answer.play_again_why: The run was decent, but the late years looped and I would want a break first. I might try a scholar start later.

tone_breaks.note: This is a big mismatch with the annual pay package of about $2.53M and the $45.5M header I noticed. The totals did not reconcile and it would not pass a ministry audit.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is really about appointments, appraisals and grades, which is where the insider details landed. The salary was a number on the screen, not the point, and I would not have called it Minister Salary.
